LINEAR REGRESSION

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

To print the cars dataset

```{r}
print(cars)
```

To fit a linear model for the data

$$
H_{0}:\beta_{1}=\beta_{2} \quad v/s \quad H_{1}:\beta_{1} = \beta_{2}
$$

```{r}
mod <- lm(dist~speed ,data=cars)
summary(mod)
```

From the summary the Multiple R-Squared illustrates that 65.11 percent of the y variable is explained by the x variable . Adjusted R-Squared is not needed for a simple linear regression and is used

The fitted regression model is

$$
E(y/x) = -17.5791 + 3.9324x
$$

From the fitted model the y intercept id -17.591 then the slope is 3.9324

To fit a scatterplot for the model

```{r}
cars %>% 
  ggplot(aes(dist,speed,fill="blue"))+ 
  geom_point(fill="green")+
  geom_smooth(method = lm,se = F)+
  theme_bw()
```

Residual is the difference of the distance of the points from the expected value

To plot the residuals and plot it to see the distribution of the residuals

```{r}
hist(mod$residuals)
```

The residuals are normally distributed

$$
\displaystyle (x-E(x)) ~ N(\mu,\sigma)
$$

To use our model to predict speeds 10,15,20

$$
E(y/x =10,15,20) \quad =-17.5791+3.9324x
$$

```{r}
new_speeds <- data.frame(speed = c(10,15,20))
predict(mod,new_speeds) %>% 
  round(1)
```
